Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue "Razor: custom snippet fields (`<Literal>` declarations) are inserted as plain text, with no tab stops" (#85988) at dotnet/roslyn
Events.RelatedBody:
**Version Used**: Visual Studio Community 2026, version 18.9.2 (Windows 11) **Steps to Reproduce**: 1. Save this as `razor-field-repro.snippet` in a folder, and add the folder in **Tools → Code Snippets Manager** under language **HTML**: ```xml
Razor field repro razor_field_repro Expansion
message Your changes were saved. $message$ $end$]]> ``` 2. Restart Visual Studio, open any `.cshtml` file, type `razor_field_repro` in markup, and commit the completion item. 3. Without moving the cursor, start typing. **Expected Behavior**: "Your changes were saved." is selected as a tab stop, and typing replaces it. This is how fields behave for the same kind of snippet in the classic HTML editor, and for C# snippets in `.cs` files. **Actual Behavior**: "Your changes were saved." is inserted as plain text, and the cursor is placed after `` (the `$end$` position). Typing goes there, and there are no tab stops to move between. **Cause**: The parser builds field parts correctly. `XmlSnippetParser.ExpansionTemplate` gives each editable field an `EditIndex`, and repeated fields share one ([source](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/ad34e675fc51beef49d66cb8005af3752895727d/src/Razor/src/Razor/src/Microsoft.VisualStudio.LanguageServices.Razor/Snippets/XmlSnippetParser.ExpansionTemplate.cs#L152)). But `SnippetCache.TryResolveSnippetString` builds the insert text from each part's `DefaultText` alone, so `SnippetFieldPart` never becomes an LSP tab stop. Only `SnippetCursorPart` contributes one (`$0`) ([source](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/ad34e675fc51beef49d66cb8005af3752895727d/src/Razor/src/Razor/src/Microsoft.VisualStudio.LanguageServices.Razor/Snippets/SnippetCache.cs#L62-L68)): ```csharp foreach (var part in parsedSnippet.Parts) { var toAppend = part is SnippetShortcutPart ? snippet.Shortcut : part.DefaultText; functionSnippetBuilder.Append(toAppend); } ``` The C# side of Roslyn's snippet support converts fields to LSP tab stops at this step ([source](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/ad34e675fc51beef49d66cb8005af3752895727d/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/InlineCompletions/InlineCompletionsHandler.cs#L211)): ```csharp var lspTextForField = string.IsNullOrEmpty(field.DefaultText) ? $"${{{field.EditIndex}}}" : $"${{{field.EditIndex}:{field.DefaultText}}}"; ``` **Suggested fix**: In `TryResolveSnippetString`, emit `${EditIndex:DefaultText}` (or `${EditIndex}` for an empty default) for a `SnippetFieldPart` with a non-null `EditIndex`. Fields with `Editable="false"` already get a null `EditIndex` and would stay plain text. Since the result is LSP snippet syntax, `$`, `}` and `\` in literal text and defaults would also need escaping. The original PR that added custom snippet support, dotnet/razor#9327, listed "No … Declarations … Literal … support" as a known limitation, with "If needed we could address each of these individually." This issue is a request to address it. Without fields, custom snippets in Razor files can only control the final cursor position. This is separate from #85331, where C# snippets don't expand in `.razor` files. That one is about C# snippets; this one is about field handling for the HTML snippets that do expand.

Events.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Merge dotnetup getting started documentation to main" (#55509) at dotnet/sdk
Events.RelatedBody:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have read the [dotnetup documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup issues](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3AArea-dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup discussions](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/discussions/categories/dotnetup).

### Issue type

Bug report

### Description

It looks like the getting started doc for dotnetup is only present in a feature branch right now.

https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup

I think this is preventing proper SEO. The above doc doesn't appear in the results for me in these searches:
- https://duckduckgo.com/?q=dotnetup+install
- https://www.google.com/search?hl=en&q=dotnetup+install

I think if this doc were merged to the main branch of this repo, then it would probably get indexed better by search engines and it would be easier to find.

This is useful if you are on a machine which doesn't have it installed, you don't remember how to install it, you're just trying to quickly figure out how.


### dotnetup version

_No response_

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy
Issues.Body:
Create a new `netstandard2.1` library.
Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy" (#1791)

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Razor: custom snippet fields (`<Literal>` declarations) are inserted as plain text, with no tab stops
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: Visual Studio Community 2026, version 18.9.2 (Windows 11) **Steps to Reproduce**: 1. Save this as `razor-field-repro.snippet` in a folder, and add the folder in **Tools → Code Snippets Manager** under language **HTML**: ```xml
Razor field repro razor_field_repro Expansion
message Your changes were saved. $message$ $end$]]> ``` 2. Restart Visual Studio, open any `.cshtml` file, type `razor_field_repro` in markup, and commit the completion item. 3. Without moving the cursor, start typing. **Expected Behavior**: "Your changes were saved." is selected as a tab stop, and typing replaces it. This is how fields behave for the same kind of snippet in the classic HTML editor, and for C# snippets in `.cs` files. **Actual Behavior**: "Your changes were saved." is inserted as plain text, and the cursor is placed after `` (the `$end$` position). Typing goes there, and there are no tab stops to move between. **Cause**: The parser builds field parts correctly. `XmlSnippetParser.ExpansionTemplate` gives each editable field an `EditIndex`, and repeated fields share one ([source](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/ad34e675fc51beef49d66cb8005af3752895727d/src/Razor/src/Razor/src/Microsoft.VisualStudio.LanguageServices.Razor/Snippets/XmlSnippetParser.ExpansionTemplate.cs#L152)). But `SnippetCache.TryResolveSnippetString` builds the insert text from each part's `DefaultText` alone, so `SnippetFieldPart` never becomes an LSP tab stop. Only `SnippetCursorPart` contributes one (`$0`) ([source](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/ad34e675fc51beef49d66cb8005af3752895727d/src/Razor/src/Razor/src/Microsoft.VisualStudio.LanguageServices.Razor/Snippets/SnippetCache.cs#L62-L68)): ```csharp foreach (var part in parsedSnippet.Parts) { var toAppend = part is SnippetShortcutPart ? snippet.Shortcut : part.DefaultText; functionSnippetBuilder.Append(toAppend); } ``` The C# side of Roslyn's snippet support converts fields to LSP tab stops at this step ([source](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/ad34e675fc51beef49d66cb8005af3752895727d/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/InlineCompletions/InlineCompletionsHandler.cs#L211)): ```csharp var lspTextForField = string.IsNullOrEmpty(field.DefaultText) ? $"${{{field.EditIndex}}}" : $"${{{field.EditIndex}:{field.DefaultText}}}"; ``` **Suggested fix**: In `TryResolveSnippetString`, emit `${EditIndex:DefaultText}` (or `${EditIndex}` for an empty default) for a `SnippetFieldPart` with a non-null `EditIndex`. Fields with `Editable="false"` already get a null `EditIndex` and would stay plain text. Since the result is LSP snippet syntax, `$`, `}` and `\` in literal text and defaults would also need escaping. The original PR that added custom snippet support, dotnet/razor#9327, listed "No … Declarations … Literal … support" as a known limitation, with "If needed we could address each of these individually." This issue is a request to address it. Without fields, custom snippets in Razor files can only control the final cursor position. This is separate from #85331, where C# snippets don't expand in `.razor` files. That one is about C# snippets; this one is about field handling for the HTML snippets that do expand.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Razor: custom snippet fields (`<Literal>` declarations) are inserted as plain text, with no tab stops" (#85988)

Issues.Title: [release/insiders] Fix analyzer collision in bootstrap leg (backport #85870)
Issues.Body:
AI-generated:

Backport of #85870 to `release/insiders`.

**Investigation (build 1623203, release/insiders @ 015578a):** `Build - Validate Correctness` failed with `Analyzer inconsistency building [...]` and then `Compilation not allowed at this time` from the bootstrap compiler server. Two versions of `System.ClientModel.SourceGeneration.dll` were loaded into one server:
- `Microsoft.Internal.VisualStudio.Shell.Framework` (VS SDK, used by VS/Razor projects such as ContainedLanguage, Benchmarks) depends on `System.ClientModel` 1.8.1.
- `Azure.Core` 1.53.0 (via `Azure.Identity` in RoslynTools) depends on `System.ClientModel` 1.10.0.

The source generator ships in the `System.ClientModel` package's analyzers folder, so different projects fed different copies of the same-identity analyzer to the server. `release/insiders` lacked the `System.ClientModel` pin that `main` has. With central transitive pinning (`CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled`), the pin forces 1.10.0 everywhere.

**Validation:** restored `Microsoft.VisualStudio.LanguageServer.ContainedLanguage.csproj` and `Microsoft.RoslynTools.csproj`; both resolve only `System.ClientModel/1.10.0`. No tests added in this first draft. CI bootstrap leg is the real check.

Issues.Title: Fix ParentTag binding for Tag Helpers inside plain HTML elements
Issues.Body:
### Summary

Fixes an issue where Razor Tag Helpers using the `ParentTag` constraint fail to bind when their immediate parent is a plain HTML element.

During unresolved element conversion and re-resolution, the compiler preserved parent context for Tag Helper elements but did not correctly propagate the context of plain HTML parent elements.

As a result, Tag Helpers with descriptors such as `[HtmlTargetElement("span", ParentTag = "div")]` were silently excluded from the generated Razor code, even when the parent constraint was satisfied.

Preserve the unresolved HTML parent context during element resolution and update `GetParentTagInfo` to recognize plain HTML parent elements. The parent tag name is passed without the configured Tag Helper prefix, ensuring correct matching when `@tagHelperPrefix` is used.

### Tests

Added integration tests covering:

- A Tag Helper with `ParentTag = "div"` correctly binds to a `<span>` nested inside a plain HTML `<div>`.
- A Tag Helper does not bind when its immediate HTML parent does not match the `ParentTag` constraint.
- A Tag Helper does not bind when only a grandparent matches the `ParentTag` constraint.
- A Tag Helper correctly binds when `@tagHelperPrefix` is configured and its immediate parent is a plain HTML element.

### Validation

- All four regression tests pass.
- Full Razor compiler test suite passes (approximately 9,300 tests).
- Verified that `ParentTag` constraints match against the immediate HTML parent rather than an ancestor.
- Verified that plain HTML parent names are handled without incorrectly applying the Tag Helper prefix.

Fixes #85971

> [!NOTE]
> AI assistance was used to help understand the existing Razor compiler test structures, and prepare this pull request description.

Issues.Title: Keep tuple element names when nullable analysis re-infers a call with a tuple literal argument
Issues.Body:
Fixes #74493

When nullable analysis re-runs method type inference (`GetArgumentsForMethodTypeInference`), a tuple literal argument is passed as its converted type. In the issue's example the converted type of `("A", "A")` is `(string, object?)`, which is the type the initial binding inferred for `T` minus the element names. Next to the other candidate, `(string Name, object? Value)`, it only differs by names, so the re-inferred `T` loses them. The lambdas passed to `ToDictionary` are then rebound against an unnamed tuple, `t.Name` and `t.Value` no longer bind, and CS8621 is reported, although the initial binding is fine.

This gives re-inference the literal as the initial binding saw it, keeping each element's nullability from flow analysis:
- a literal with a natural type is passed with that type;
- a literal without one, e.g. `("A", null)`, is passed as the typeless literal with its elements' flow types.

This follows the approach discussed in the issue, as is already done for lambdas and collection expressions.

Tests cover a literal without names, with matching names, with different names (only CS8123, as in the initial binding), without a natural type, nested tuples, and non-literal tuple arguments. Four of them fail on main and all pass with the change. The full `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Semantic.UnitTests` run passes locally (19823 passed, 0 failed).

Issues.Title: Don't include the zero member when formatting a flags enum TypedConstant
Issues.Body:
Fixes #74326

`TypedConstant.ToCSharpString()` and `ToVisualBasicString()` build the bitwise-or form of a flags enum value by adding every member whose bits are all set in the value. A member with value 0 always passes that check, so `FlagEnum.Flag1 | FlagEnum.Flag3` came out as `FlagEnum.None | FlagEnum.Flag1 | FlagEnum.Flag3`.

This skips zero-valued members when building the bitwise-or form, in the signed and unsigned paths of both languages. A value of 0 still matches `None` exactly and is shown as `FlagEnum.None`.

Added `ToCSharpString_FlagsEnum_ExcludesZeroMember` and `ToVisualBasicString_FlagsEnum_ExcludesZeroMember` covering signed and unsigned underlying types. Both fail without the change (`E.None | E.A | E.C`) and pass with it. `TypedConstantTests` passes in both Symbol test projects.

Issues.Title: Fix symbol-completion publication races
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes dotnet/roslyn#85950.

Add acquire semantics to symbol-completion readiness checks that publish data
stored in separate fields. Interlocked writers already order the payload before
the completion marker; an ordinary reader can nevertheless observe completion
without observing the payload on a weakly ordered architecture.

Use volatile backing fields with narrowly scoped CS0420 suppressions where
appropriate, and the existing `Volatile.Read` /
`RoslynImmutableInterlocked.VolatileRead` helpers otherwise. Preserve lazy
initialization, publication order, and the existing single-winner protocols.

## Scope

The fourteen commits keep each issue family independently reviewable:

- Shared custom-attribute bag completion.
- Source namespace/named-type member sorting; VB signatures, constraints,
  event inference, and default-property-name publication.
- PE field signatures, resolved type-parameter bounds/use-site information,
  explicit class overrides, attribute constructors, and hidden parameter
  attributes.
- Script-field inference, local-function return-type diagnostics, and assembly
  duplicate-attribute side tables.

The PE-field changes protect separately stored ref-kind/modifier/volatile and
fixed-buffer state (C#), and custom modifiers (VB). Returning the type itself
through the published type reference does not require this additional acquire.

No public APIs, resources, or diagnostics changed. No test changes are included.

## Validation

Existing targeted symbol tests were run with
`-c Release -f net10.0 --no-restore -p:RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true`:

| Project | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C# Symbol.UnitTests | 75 | 2 existing skips | 0 |
| VB Symbol.UnitTests | 249 | 0 | 0 |

Inspected generated Release IL at all 24 changed readiness gates, including the
immutable-array helper's read barrier. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
The agent-documentation assessment required no changes.

Validation was performed on x64. No ARM64 hardware reproduction or
failure-before/pass-after stress-test result is claimed; the existing tests
provide compatibility coverage, while the ordering fixes were checked against
the publication protocols and generated IL.

Issues.Title: Fix daemon telemetry isolation test race
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/85947.

The initialization RPC can return before its request telemetry scope is disposed. A metric sink registered after client creation can therefore receive legitimate late initialization measurements, making the second server's zero-measurement assertion race.

This test-only change records metric event names and tags, waits for the hover request counter after fault reporting, and asserts hover-specific isolation after the first server exits. Production telemetry behavior is unchanged.

Issues.Title: Also filter out methods hidden by non-browsable methods in completion
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Clean rework of #85816. That pull request accumulated review-driven complexity and is obsolete; this replaces it.

When completion removes a method because it is `[EditorBrowsable(Never)]`, also remove the base methods it hides, so they do not show up in its place (for example `object.Equals(object, object)` hidden by `new static Equals`).

The filter hides by signature only. `HidesBaseMethodsByName` is not consulted: it is always true for VB and never true for C# source, so it only describes non-C# metadata. The behavior is documented against https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/4434#issuecomment-546428317.

- Walk base types with `GetMembers(name)` instead of rescanning the completion symbol list.
- `EditorBrowsable(Advanced)` does not also remove the base method.
- Interface lookup includes base interfaces and `object`.

Fixes #4434

## Test plan

- [x] `EditorBrowsable_Method_BrowsableState*` completion tests (12 passed locally), covering metadata `Equals` hidden by `new static Equals`, a different-signature overload that stays visible, `Advanced` not hiding the base method, interface and `object` members, and an extension method that does not hide an instance method.

Issues.Title: Handle ref field dereference failures without aborting expansion
Issues.Body: ## Summary Expanding a ref struct with an uninitialized ref field can cause the debugger’s `Dereference` call to throw `InvalidOperationException`. This aborts member expansion, leaving `...` in the debugger window and preventing inspection of the remaining fields. Catch this exception at the individual member and return a failed evaluation result containing the debugger’s error message. The remaining fields continue to expand normally. This displays a field evaluation error rather than synthesizing a `NullReferenceException` result. ## Tests Added ResultProvider tests covering: - A ref field returned as an exception result, with its sibling field still displayed. - A ref field whose dereference throws `InvalidOperationException`, with an error displayed for that field and its sibling still displayed. A per-value override in the test mock reproduces the throwing dereference observed in Visual Studio. ## Validation - Both regression tests pass on `net10.0`. - Analyzer-enabled build completes without warnings. - Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. - Manually verified in RoslynDev that Watch expands the struct, displays an error for the uninitialized ref field, and displays the ordinary field’s value as `10`. Fixes #85800 ### Before: ### After: > [!NOTE] > AI assistance was used to help understand the existing test structure and reproduce the issue and to prepare this pull request description. ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/85967)

Issues.Title: Introduce a Razor DLL for `dotnet format`, and share formatting code
Issues.Body:
Part of https://github.com/dotnet/format/issues/153

**Preamble**

I know this looks big, but I did the commits in a very deliberate order to make it really easy to review commit-at-a-time. Up to about the 4th last commit everything is essentially mechanical moves, and I made sure to do them separate to renames as much as possible to make it easy. Thank you for your patience.

**The explanation seam (or slice, you choose)**

The aim here is to allow `dotnet format` to format Razor files. It won't be able to format `script` or `style` tag contents, because there is no Html language server available, but it should be able to do the rest. In order to do that we need the Razor formatter code to be available in the SDK, hence the creation of a Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Razor.DotNetFormat.dll. In order to not duplicate code, this also creates two new shared projects, one for code from MS.CA.Razor.Workspaces, and one for the actual formatting code. MS.CA.Razor.Workspaces can't just be shipped as a dependency because it depends on the Roslyn language server, and that is a large can of worms.

The shared projects are a _little_ bigger than necessary, in that they don't contain just the extension methods that are actually used by the formatter, but that makes the review much easier and means there is still only one place to put future methods. There is a little quirk of an `LSP` define that allows the shared methods to use LSP types, but its very lightly used, so I think its all a worthy trade-off.

Issues.Title: dotnetup: Use simpler process creation APIs
Issues.Body:
[SelfUpdateVerifier](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/dnup/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/SelfUpdate/SelfUpdateVerifier.cs) has  a lot of complicated Process handling code in it.

.NET 11 has new Process APIs which should drastically simplify this: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/process-api-improvements-in-dotnet-11/

My copilot thinks that we can replace this code with a single call: `Process.RunAndCaptureTextAsync(startInfo, cancellationToken)`, and all we lose is the 4KB output buffer limit.  If we still need that limit we can use other newer APIs to still simplify the code a bunch, but I don't think the output limit is worth the complexity for an updated executable that we've already validated the hash for.

There may be other places in the code where we should also switch to the new APIs, for example:

Issues.Title: Prepare workload marker and root shim layouts for incremental builds
Issues.Body:
## Problem

Full installer builds currently delete and recreate the staging directory. Before we can remove that deletion, each layout target needs to clean up the old files it owns.

The workload marker and root shim targets don't do that today. Reusing a layout can leave old feature-band markers, markers after source-only mode is disabled, or launchers that no longer belong in that layout.

## Changes

- Remove obsolete `userlocal` markers without deleting workload records or other metadata.
- Remove obsolete root `dnx` and `dnx.cmd` files from base and intermediate installer staging, keeping the existing platform rules.
- Use the same preparation and completion pattern as the template and manifest layouts to skip unchanged work and recover from missing outputs or interrupted builds.
- Validate checked owned paths before cleanup, and restore shim contents if archive extraction has replaced the SDK's script.

This establishes the cleanup rules needed by #55871, which will replace the broad staging-directory deletion. **That deletion remains in this PR, so this is groundwork for incremental builds, not a significant full-build speedup.**

Fixes: #55870

Issues.Title: Harden agentic workflow assignment, unlock, and detection
Issues.Body:
## Why

The reported agentic workflow failures come from three different boundaries: valid assignment outputs are rejected by an invalid PAT, a transient GitHub API failure leaves an issue locked, and detection reports failures when there are no outputs to inspect. OpenAI Responses also rejects Copilot CLI edit-tool identifiers during analysis and detection.

Related to #56558, #56550, #56514, #56549, and #56519. These are not closing references: credential recovery and hosted verification remain outstanding, and #56519 is an automatically managed detection tracker.

## Approach

- Authenticate `ISSUE_MONSTER_ASSIGNMENT_TOKEN` before activation and inference, without falling back to inference-only PATs. Preserve the handler's actual assignment confirmation.
- Retry transient unlock failures three times in the existing privileged job, only for an issue locked by the current activation. Permanent HTTP errors remain terminal.
- Skip the build-failure detector job only when the agent produced neither safe outputs nor a patch. Outputs and patches still undergo normal detection.
- Use `claude-sonnet-5` for the Issue Monster detector and as the build-failure analyzer default, preserving analyzer model-variable overrides. This is a compatibility mitigation for the upstream `ctc_call`/`fc` serialization error, not a repair of that upstream defect.

Includes source and generated-workflow regression tests, troubleshooting guidance, and five regenerated workflow lock files.

## Validation

35 focused Node tests pass (exit 0):

```powershell
node --test .github\scripts\agentic-workflow-guards.test.js .github\scripts\issue-monster-search.test.js .github\ci-quality-monitor\test\workflow-policy.test.mjs
```

All five affected workflows pass strict compilation and source validation with gh-aw v0.89.21 (exit 0):

```powershell
gh aw compile issue-monster-assigner issue-triage issue-monster build-failure-analysis build-failure-analysis-command --strict --no-check-update --schedule-seed dotnet/sdk --action-mode action --action-tag v0.89.21 --validate --no-emit
```

The tests exercise inline scripts with mocked API boundaries, the compiled dependency graph, and detector conditions. Native actionlint 1.7.12 reports the same 22 unsupported-syntax findings on the baseline and patch, with no new findings; this is not a clean lint result. Shellcheck reports existing SC2004 notes in PAT selection. Documentation links and `git diff --check` pass.

## Operational follow-up

`ISSUE_MONSTER_ASSIGNMENT_TOKEN` returned HTTP 401 in all three reported assignment runs. An administrator must renew it with metadata: read and actions, contents, issues, and pull requests: write for `dotnet/sdk`; this patch cannot repair the secret. The new preflight verifies authentication and repository read access, not assignment write permissions.

No manual hosted reruns were dispatched. Actual assignment recovery, hosted unlock retries, and output-producing model compatibility still require end-to-end verification. Existing issue locks were not changed.

Issues.Title: `dotnetup`: make the download cache process- and cross-process-safe
Issues.Body:
## Problem

`DownloadCache` is not coordinated across the multiple cache objects and processes that use the same dotnetup download-cache directory.

Each `DotnetArchiveDownloader` currently constructs its own `DownloadCache`. Each cache instance loads `cache-index.json` once into an instance-local dictionary, and the lock added around that dictionary only coordinates calls on that one object. Production can have multiple instances through parallel batch installs, background predownload overlapping installation, and multiple dotnetup processes.

A stale read-modify-write can lose mappings without requiring simultaneous writes:

1. Cache A and Cache B both load an empty index.
2. A adds URL A and writes `{ A }`.
3. B adds URL B using its stale dictionary and writes `{ B }`.
4. The archive for A remains on disk, but its mapping is gone and the file is orphaned.

Concurrent writers can also lose updates when one index write fails, publish invalid JSON, or bypass the filename-collision check using stale state. Archive hash verification prevents this from becoming a trust bypass, but it causes duplicate downloads, unreliable predownload reuse, and orphaned cache files.

This is a pre-existing cache issue identified while reviewing #56507; that PR does not introduce the stale-index design.

## Proposed direction

After #55511 merges, reuse its path-scoped `ScopedLockFile` / `LockFileRetryPolicy` primitives for a permanent lock such as `<downloadcache>/downloadcache.lock`.

The desired model is:

- Make the default cache process-shared per canonical cache-directory path, without requiring a `DownloadCache` instance to be propagated through every installer/extractor/downloader constructor. A path-keyed singleton/factory is preferred. Pub/sub invalidation could keep multiple in-process views synchronized, but the file lock and disk reload must remain authoritative for cross-process safety.
- Under the short exclusive cache lock, reload the current index, merge the update, publish archive files through unique temporary paths and atomic rename, and atomically replace the index through a same-directory temporary file.
- Cache reads must observe updates made by another instance/process. Prefer encapsulating lookup plus hard-link/copy materialization in the cache so another writer cannot change the selected path between those operations.
- Do not hold the cache lock during network download or archive hashing. Duplicate downloads are acceptable; corrupted or lost cache state is not.
- Cache lock contention or timeout should degrade to a cache miss / skipped cache write rather than fail an otherwise valid installation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Production callers using the same canonical directory share one in-process cache by default without plumbing a cache object through each layer.
- Two independently-created cache clients preserve both mappings after interleaved writes.
- Separate dotnetup processes preserve mappings and cannot corrupt `cache-index.json`.
- A live cache client observes an entry published by another client/process.
- Filename collision handling remains correct across instances and processes.
- Index publication is atomic and failed cache operations do not fail installation.
- Tests cover multiple cache objects and child-process contention, not only concurrent calls on one object.
- Existing signed-manifest and archive SHA-512 verification behavior is unchanged.

## Related

- #55511 introduces the scoped file-lock and retry primitives proposed for reuse.
- #56507 modifies archive-cache materialization and is where this pre-existing race was identified.

Issues.Title: Produce `daily` and `preview` stamped `dotnetup` builds in one CI
Issues.Body:
Resolves https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/55584

The [pipeline run](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3100135&view=results) demonstrates that in the artifacts:
1. Two `dotnetup` builds are produced now - a `daily` and `preview` build, from the same CI
2. If you download each, you will see that `dotnetup --info` or `dotnetup list` will now show the correct `-daily` or `-preview` suffix in its version / assembly information, where as before, it would always be `preview`.
3. Production runs automatically publish the daily candidate; preview promotion remains manual. Both use one complete manifest and the optional `BlobAssetIdPattern` regex proposed in dotnet/arcade#17684. Test runs only print the daily promotion command and do not publish or promote either candidate.

The reason we are doing 2 builds is remarked in the issue above, but basically we don't want to require a rebuild of what we already validated when we promote something from daily to preview. Also, we don't want to maintain 2 branches. When stable happens, we will take on that burden.

Version semantics and release policy is already defined - this PR is not meant for a discussion board on what has already been decided.

It may be confusing that the `sdk` pipeline is also in the change list, however, this does not impact SDK publishing. The two share the same overall template.

The latest change removes `PrepareCandidateAssetIds.cs`, the custom registration project/script, selector files, and their synthetic-manifest tests. Registration now uses Arcade's standard `PublishBuildAssets` task and uploads its complete `MergedManifest.xml` as `AssetManifests`. Daily and preview publishing pass a regex selecting that quality's blobs and the shared archived manifest; `%7C` safely forwards regex alternation through MSBuild. `BuildQuality` controls only the destination links, while `BlobAssetIdPattern` controls which blobs are published. BAR inventory and channel membership remain build-wide.

Daily versions omit the preview iteration (`0.2.0-daily.26508.2`); preview versions retain it (`0.2.0-preview.1.26508.2`).

The promotion pipeline must consume dotnet/arcade#17684 before production promotion can work. This PR is deliberately authored against that proposed contract without changing the Arcade dependency pin.

Latest local validation:
- 12 actual MSBuild version-regression tests passed, covering all three dotnetup projects, both qualities, and preview iterations 0, 1, 2, and 10.
- 74 retained version-sanitizer/architecture-sync tests passed; builds had no warnings or errors.
- Daily/preview regex checks selected 20 candidate blobs plus the shared archive from the 41-blob test inventory, with no opposite-quality blobs or inventory changes.
- YAML, XML, PowerShell 7/Windows PowerShell 5.1, MSBuild regex escaping, print-only test promotion, and documentation-link checks passed.

The linked CI run predates this publishing simplification and the omission of the daily iteration. Real signing, publication, promotion, and aka.ms updates have not been validated by these latest local checks.

Issues.Title: Remove unused native CLI task resources and trim off-platform detection providers
Issues.Body:
## Rationale and size-driven scope decision

Native AOT cannot infer every invariant of the SDK's native command closure. This PR retains only two optimizations: excluding unused MSBuild-task diagnostic resources and constructing internal detection providers only on their supported platforms. Managed fallback and supported behavior remain unchanged.

The broader experiment measured each optimization by disabling only that change from the same Windows x64 Release build, with full CLI string tables retained:

| Optimization | Marginal native-library saving | Final decision |
|---|---:|---|
| Exclude unused task diagnostic resources | 776,704 bytes (758.5 KiB) | Keep |
| Platform-specific detection-provider construction | 17,920 bytes (17.5 KiB) | Keep |
| Substitute unreachable certificate trust | 4,608 bytes (4.5 KiB) | Removed |
| XML-only output-method substitution | 51,200 bytes (50 KiB) | Removed |

These are one-at-a-time marginal deltas, not additive attribution. The broader implementation saved 848,384 bytes (4.25%); its marginal deltas sum 2,048 bytes higher because native layout/alignment/shared dependencies are non-additive.

The earlier scope selection was corrected at the author's request: retain platform-specific providers rather than certificate trust. All certificate/XML substitution descriptors and wiring are now removed. This PR introduces no ILC method substitutions.

### Final implementation size

Matched Windows x64 Release native-library measurements, with full CLI string tables and ASP.NET support included:

| Build | Native library bytes |
|---|---:|
| Baseline | 19,943,424 |
| Task-resource exclusion + platform-specific providers | 19,149,824 |
| **Net saving** | **793,600 bytes (775 KiB, 3.98%)** |

This measures `dotnet-aot.dll`, not the full SDK/archive. Bootstrap SDK: `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`; runtime/ILC packages: `12.0.0-alpha.1.26480.102`. Other platforms were not measured locally.

## Retained changes and why automatic trimming could not remove them

- Remove the unused task `Strings.resx` input from the native source list. Explicit embedding and runtime resource-name lookup prevent automatic removal even though the native closure does not execute its consumers. Managed/out-of-process task assemblies retain their resources.
- Guard production detection-provider construction with direct `OperatingSystem` intrinsics, which ILC can evaluate for the target platform. Previously all providers were constructed before virtual support checks against an injectable context, rooting off-platform implementations. Preserve common providers and registration order, Linux WSL providers and Windows-data parsers, and the all-platform injected-context factory for tests. Change its options factory from eager static initialization to an on-demand property so it does not root all providers in production.
- Keep native resource/provider regression tests and maintenance guidance in `src/Cli/AGENTS.md`, the AOT command skill, and `dotnet-aot/DESIGN.md`. New command paths and providers must revisit resource exclusions, platform gates, WSL requirements, and static initialization roots.

Full CLI string tables/cultures remain. Dynamic resource scanning and checked-in subset experiments have been reverted. Resource-removal descriptors remove whole manifest resources, not individual keys in a mixed-use table. No certificate, XML, or Azure credential substitutions remain.

## Validation

Final corrected implementation: clean Windows x64 Release product publish and native test publish succeeded. **186 native tests passed, zero failures or skips**, using the freshly published product library. Resource exclusion and platform provider regressions are included. The native compiler response file contains no substitution arguments. The Windows dependency graph excludes macOS SSO and WSL workplace-join providers, retains the Windows workplace-join provider, and again includes the original Windows certificate trust implementation. Skill validation, local documentation-link checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Existing test-only Native AOT warning rollups remain unchanged; no suppressions were added.

Linux/macOS native execution, full redist integration, and managed CLI regression-project validation have not run locally. No supported user-visible behavior is intentionally changed.

Issues.Title: APICompat CP0023 fails for ExperimentalAttribute differences across target frameworks
Issues.Body:
### Description
Building the source-build-assets reference package `Microsoft.Bcl.Cryptography` with the .NET 12 SDK fails package API compatibility validation with CP0023. The validator compares `lib/netstandard2.1/Microsoft.Bcl.Cryptography.dll` with `lib/net8.0/Microsoft.Bcl.Cryptography.dll` and reports APIs as previously stable in the former but experimental in the latter.

The net8.0 reference surface marks the ML-DSA/ML-KEM APIs with `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.Experimental("SYSLIB5006")`; the netstandard2.1 surface does not. This appears to be due to the ExperimentalAttribute not being available to that downlevel target, rather than a signature or implementation change. The same class of diagnostics also appears for package versions 10.0.3 and 10.0.4.

### Reproduction
Build `src/referencePackages/src/microsoft.bcl.cryptography/10.0.10/Microsoft.Bcl.Cryptography.10.0.10.csproj` with package validation enabled using SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102`.

### Expected behavior
Package validation should allow this target-framework-specific Experimental annotation difference, or provide a supported way to represent/suppress it without disabling the package's other API compatibility checks.

### Actual behavior
The build fails with CP0023 for the affected APIs, causing both Windows and Linux `source-build-assets-CI` jobs to fail.

### Related PR
https://github.com/dotnet/source-build-assets/pull/1818

Issues.Title: [dnceng-bot] Branch `sdk/release/8.0.4xx` can't be merged to Azdo internal branch
Issues.Body:
Branch [release/8.0.4xx](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/commits/release/8.0.4xx/) in `dotnet/sdk` repo can't be mirrored from GitHub to Azure [internal/release/8.0.4xx](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-sdk?version=GBinternal%2Frelease%2F8.0.4xx&_a=history) via internal merge. 

There are conflicting commits in the target branch.
The branch is configured to be mirrored via automated merge. 
The situation is rare but normal. The target branch is expected to receive manual commits in the Azure DevOps clone, which could cause conflict.

Conflicts need to be **resolved to unblock the code flow**.

- you can resolve the issue by resolving the conflict in the **target branch only**. 
    - Please make sure that the changes sensitive from security perspective are not published ahead of time to GitHub!
- reverting the extra commits in the Azdo target branch.
- checking the logs of the mirroring process in the [mirroring pipeline](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build?definitionId=1387).
- you can disable the mirroring of the branch in the [configuration file](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/dnceng-subscriptions.jsonc).
- you can ask @dotnet/dnceng for help or read the [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/README.md).

Please close this issue once the conflict is resolved.

Issues.Title: .NET 11 Release Candidate 1
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Body: # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS > This issue is a locked mirror of dotnet/core/discussions/10480. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Preview 7. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/preview7).

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/dotnetmaui.md)

- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/msbuild.md)

- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-62900 | .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git and Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Improper removal of sensitive information before storage or transfer in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sourcelink/issues/1757 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-212: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### Published NuGet packages Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 The affected packages used by .NET 8 and .NET 9 SDKs are built with SDK-specific prerelease versions that aren't published as stable NuGet packages. Update to SDK 8.0.130 or 8.0.424, SDK 9.0.120 or 9.0.317, or SDK 10.0.111 or 10.0.303 to receive the fix. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK (Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A tampering vulnerability exists in the .NET SDK (.NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10) container image build process which could allow a local attacker to inject resources that could be incorporated into container images built by other users on the same machine. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/55274 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.28 | 8.0.29 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable nuget package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.29 Runtime or .NET 8.0.129 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.18 Runtime or .NET 9.0.316 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.10 Runtime or .NET 10.0.302 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.
